advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a precheck-unit case with a bug plan that WOULD block (no `## Acceptance Criteria`) and assert `det_blocking == []` AND the P1 block now appears in `det_advisory`.
evidence: _state default `description=_BUG_DESC` includes `## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] Y no longer happens...` (test_bug_review_tier.py:34-39), so P1 passes and no DET block is produced.
p1_readiness_shape only blocks when `_count_ac_items(text) < 1` (det_floor.py:163-190) — with AC present there is nothing to downgrade.

workflow_ops bug arm sets `det_blocking=[]` AND `det_advisory=[*det_blocks, *det_advisories]` (workflow_ops.py:171-177), but the test asserts only `det_blocking == []`, never that a would-be block landed in det_advisory.
Contrast: the e2e workflow test test_bug_runs_light_advisory_tier_not_exempt uses a no-AC bug description, so the full downgrade path IS covered there — the gap is unit-level assertion strength.
advisory.finding: The precheck-unit 'never blocked' test cannot detect a regression in the DET-block downgrade: it uses a plan WITH `## Acceptance Criteria`, so run_det_floor yields no blocking finding and `det_blocking == []` holds trivially even if the downgrade logic were removed; it also never asserts the downgraded block appears in `det_advisory`.
scenarios: A refactor that stops populating det_advisory with the downgraded blocks
A regression where a bug's DET block is no longer downgraded to advisory
